text:
lina: Hey team — I'm onboarding and hitting a weird network thing. I can SSH to bastion, but pulls from our internal Docker registry (registry.internal.redwood:5000) fail when I'm on the company VPN with split-tunnel enabled. curl just hangs. Anyone seen this? 🙏

sandeep: Hi Lina — welcome! This is pretty common with split-tunnel + Docker because Docker's daemon doesn't inherit your shell proxy. Quick test: can you run curl from your laptop (not from inside Docker) with the bastion SOCKS proxy?

lina: I tried `curl http://registry.internal.redwood:5000/v2/_catalog` and it times out. SSH to bastion works: `ssh ec2-user@bastion.redwood`. I haven't tried SOCKS yet.

sandeep: Try a dynamic port forward and curl via socks5h: `ssh -D 1080 -N ec2-user@bastion.redwood` then in another shell:

```
export ALL_PROXY=socks5h://localhost:1080
curl -v http://registry.internal.redwood:5000/v2/_catalog
```
If that succeeds, the issue is Docker/daemon-level routing.

amanda: Also for Docker you can either configure systemd drop-in for the docker.service to set the proxy env vars or add a daemon.json with proxy settings. Example daemon.json: 

```
{
  "proxies": {
    "default": {
      "httpProxy": "socks5h://localhost:1080",
      "noProxy": "localhost,127.0.0.1,::1"
    }
  }
}
```
Note: some Docker versions don't support socks proxies in daemon.json — if that fails, use `ssh -L` to forward a local TCP port to the registry via the bastion and point Docker to that.

lina: Ran the ssh -D + curl test — curl returns the catalog listing. So it's definitely Docker/daemon related.

sandeep: Cool. Two options: 1) Ask infra to add the registry to corporate route so split-tunnel sends registry traffic through the VPN; 2) Use local forwarding as a workaround. For local forwarding: `ssh -L 5000:registry.internal.redwood:5000 ec2-user@bastion.redwood` then point your local Docker to `localhost:5000`.

jonathan: Another note — if your laptop is on macOS, the Docker Desktop app runs a VM and the proxy/env handling can be quirky. If you go the `ssh -L` route, make sure Docker is actually hitting your localhost endpoint (try `curl` from inside a container or use `docker run --rm curlimages/curl curl -v http://host.docker.internal:5000/v2/_catalog`).

lina: Thanks — `ssh -L` worked for me, I can pull images now. For long-term, who should I ping to request the registry route change? @network or infra?

sandeep: Ping @network for routing policy first, then infra for firewall/proxy config. I'll create a quick ticket if you want.

amanda: Tagging this in the onboarding doc: add note about Docker + split-tunnel and two workarounds (SSH SOCKS + SSH local forward). 

devops-bot: New onboarding assist ticket created: ONB-7892 (sandeep -> network infra).

lina: Awesome — thanks everyone! Saved my day :tada:

jonathan: If you get stuck later, drop the exact `docker pull` error here or ping eng-sre.
